Latin word

versor

versor, versārī, versātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent; with cum and the ablative, or inter and the accusative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

spend time with, move among, associate with; be engaged in, be busy with, be active in

In this lexicon

  • associate

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 7.8: cum hīs versāre, quī tē meliōrem factūrī sunt; Cic. Cat. 1.10: nōbīscum versārī jam diūtius nōn potes

  • be involved

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 12.25: quī in rē pūblicā versantur (Lewis & Short s.v. reprehēnsiō); Traupman 92; Traupman 285; Traupman 334

Examples

  • Cum hīs versāre, quī tē meliōrem factūrī sunt. Illōs admitte, quōs tū potes facere meliōrēs. Mūtuō ista fīunt, et hominēs, dum docent, discunt.

    Spend your time with those who will make you better; let in those whom you can make better. It works both ways: people learn while they teach.Sen. Ep. 7.8

    In the entry for associate

  • A. Trebōniō, quī in tuā prōvinciā magna negōtia et ampla et expedīta habet, multōs annōs ūtor valdē familiāriter

    Aulus Trebonius, who has large and well-run business interests in your province, has been a close friend of mine for many yearsCic. Fam. 1.3.1
